title: Pricing impact framework for MSA/DPA indemnity tiering and liability caps
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define a repeatable experiment and rollout plan that quantifies price elasticity and sales velocity impact from offering discrete indemnity/liability tiers in MSA/DPA negotiations. We need a pragmatic way to: (1) map contract redline risk to a small set of standardized liability/indemnity tiers; (2) translate tier selection into deterministic price deltas and self-serve/auto-approve gates for sales; (3) measure legal review throughput and revenue impact so we can optimize trade-offs between revenue and legal exposure.

Scope: Enterprise MSA/DPA redlines that change indemnity language, liability caps, and escrow/third-party indemnity obligations. Includes updating quote UI, sales playbooks, and contract templates. Also touches the security questionnaire flow when indemnity relates to data breach obligations.

Out of scope: Full legal policy rewrite; bespoke regulatory waivers (e.g., exports) that require exec escalation. Non-contractual commercial discounts not tied to redlines are out of scope for this experiment iteration.

Primary stakeholders: Product (Aisha, Liam), Legal (Mariana Gomez), Sales Ops (Carlos Rivera), Revenue Ops (Priya Nair), Security & Compliance (Jasper Liu), Finance (Olivia Martin).

Success metrics (primary):
- Change in win rate for proposal bundles offering Tier A/B/C vs control (+/- baseline)
- Median days-to-contract from first quote to signed SAAS agreement (goal: reduce legal cycle for auto-approvable tiers by 25%)
- Average revenue uplift per closed deal where higher indemnity is purchased
- Number of redline escalations avoided via auto-approve rules

Monitoring & dashboards: Add Experiment board in Looker/Redash: conversion funnel, time-to-sign, legal review load, incremental revenue. Link in artifacts.

Decision principle: Prefer conservative pricing nudges and automation for low-medium risk redlines to reduce legal cycle time; reserve manual review for high-risk indemnity changes with high legal exposure.

Notes on novelty vs existing playbooks: Prior docs addressed routing and triage. This ticket couples that triage output to explicit pricing signals and sales UI changes, plus experiment telemetry to measure elasticity. That integration is what differentiates this work from previous routing/playbook efforts.
acceptance_criteria: Risk-to-price mapping documented and approved by Legal and Finance (Tier definitions + example redlines)

Auto-approve gating rules implemented for low-risk tier in the contract automation pipeline
Experiment dashboard with baseline and live cohorts tracking win rate, time-to-sign, and revenue uplift
Rollout playbook published: how Sales uses tiers, standard objection responses, and legal escalation flow
